units.translation: You will learn, being old, that it is hard for one of your age to be taught.
Alas, you have spoken to our utter ruin (thus Bamberger; M has ενπασ' with a dot above the v) — how we are being destroyed.
This cloak bears witness for me, how Aegisthus' sword dyed it.
He is arranging the death of his child, how he perished by his own hand.
He had prophesied that not by force nor against the strong should he prevail, but by guile to overcome those who were superior.
He said to your son Xerxes these things, that the Greeks would not remain, but would save their lives.
And he shouts in the syllables of letters that not even Ares could cast them from the towers.
For if he had sent me beneath the earth to Tartarus, so that neither of gods nor of men would rejoice at these things (thus Elmsley for ἐπεγήθει).
Will you not hasten to cast bonds around him, so that your father may not see you lingering?
Listen, so that you may learn the whole matter to the end.
Be at ease, so that you may not make the citizens ill-hearted.
Fulfill our prayers, so that the city may prosper.
Hasten, so that I may be blameless in time.
I pray to obtain a timely blow, so that without convulsion I may close this eye.
He was mutilated, so that you may know this.
The ruling woman ordered Aegisthus to summon the strangers as quickly as possible, so that he might learn this report more clearly.
Speak again, so that I may learn more clearly.
But bid him come himself, so that he may hear without fear.
Show the covering of the man, so that his father may see.
Decide, so that I may tell these things.
I said that she was such, so that the people might be stung.
I will not weary of telling you the good things, so that you may never say.
So that I may not become a slave to the race of Aegyptus.
Place it, so that they may see the proof of this arrival.
For such a transgression they must pay the penalty to the gods, so that he may be taught.
Go out to the deep meadow of Lerna, so that the eye of Zeus may cease from longing.
Cast my words into your heart, so that you may learn the ends of the road.
Let a purple-strewn path be made at once, so that Justice may lead him to an unexpected house.
Let us stand out of the way, so that I may learn clearly.
I praise hiding these my agreements, so that they may be caught.
But, so that you may know, for not —.
Send attendants, so that we may find the altars of the city-holding gods.
I will persuade the common people, so that I may make them well-disposed.
So that knowing I may speak more clearly.
Some wishing to cast Cronus from his seat, so that Zeus might rule, forsooth, and others hastening the opposite, so that Zeus might never rule over the gods.
He sent prophets, so that he might learn what was necessary —.
They left them casting lots, so that each of them, having obtained by lot, might lead his company to the gates.
They appointed spear-bearers, so that I might have an honored prize.
So to speak.
To speak clearly.
In a word,
She carries beneath her one man of the Cadmeans, so that many missiles may be hurled at this man.
Such a calamity of suffering came upon them, so as to outweigh these things even twice in the balance.
So that the city of the Persians may groan.
So that neither great nor any of the young may escape the great net of slavery.
So that many things from my dim mind make me groan.
